name: get_document
description: Read the document that is open in Kanvas: file path, current selection, groups, and the layer tree. Call this first, and again whenever the user may have edited by hand. Each node has id, kind, name, x, y, w, h plus its non-default properties (same names as in create_nodes; `constraints` is listed when it is not left / top; `layout` on a frame with auto layout; `sizing` and `absolute` on nodes where they are set). Top-level nodes use canvas coordinates; children of a frame are relative to that frame's top-left corner, at every nesting depth (frames can contain frames). Array order is stacking order: later = on top; in a frame with `layout` it is also the order of the items (first = leftmost / top), and their x / y are where the layout put them. For very large documents children are omitted (child_count) — pass `ids` to read specific nodes in full. Components: a main component is a frame with `component: true`; an instance of it is a frame with `instance_of` (the id of its main), and each layer inside an instance has `source` (the id of the layer of the main that it mirrors).

ids.description: Only return these nodes (in full, including children and path points). Omit for the whole document.

name: create_nodes
description:
Create layers in Kanvas. The user sees them appear immediately; the whole call is one undo step. Returns the new ids with measured sizes (text w/h are measured with the real font).

Structure: only frames can contain other nodes, and frames can be nested to any depth (a frame inside a frame is a container that clips its content, e.g. a card or a section). Put children either in a frame's `children` array, or pass `parent` (frame id, at any depth) to add to an existing frame. Children x/y are relative to the top-left of their own parent frame; children are clipped to the frame. Array order = stacking order (later = on top). Auto layout: give a frame `layout` and it places its children itself, in array order, so they need no x / y (see below) — prefer it for anything that is a row, a column or a list (buttons, cards, menus, forms, tag clouds): sizes then follow the content and nothing has to be computed by hand. A top-level node without x/y is placed in free space to the right of existing content.

Kinds and properties:
- frame: x, y, w, h, fill, stroke, children, component (true makes it a main component: a reusable element whose instances follow its changes), layout (auto layout, see below). An artboard (e.g. 1080x1080 post, 390x844 phone, 1440x900 desktop), or, inside another frame, a container that clips its content.
- rect: x, y, w, h, fill, stroke, stroke_width, radius.
- ellipse: x, y, w, h, fill, stroke, stroke_width.
- line: x, y = start; w, h = vector to the end point (may be negative or 0); stroke, stroke_width, cap.
- text: x, y (top-left), text (\n for line breaks), font (any Google Fonts family, default Inter), weight (100-900), italic, font_size, fill (text color), line_height (% of font size, 0 = auto), letter_spacing (% of font size), align (left|center|right|justify; justify stretches every line but the last of a paragraph to the box width and needs wrap:true), wrap, underline, strikethrough (both for the whole text), list (none|bullet|numbered: every paragraph, split on \n, gets a marker and a hanging indent; the markers are drawn, never write them into `text`), fixed_height, valign (top|middle|bottom). With wrap:false (default) the box hugs the text and w/h are ignored. With wrap:true the text wraps inside width w. The height follows the lines unless fixed_height:true: then the box keeps its h, valign places the lines in it, and lines that do not fit run out of it. To center text in an area, use wrap:true + w = area width + align:center. `spans` restyles character ranges: [{start, end (exclusive, character indices), font?, weight?, italic?, size?, fill?, underline?, strikethrough?}]. Text on a path: on_path (the id of an existing path, line, ellipse or rect on the page; null takes the text off again) makes the text one line that runs along that shape, each letter turned to the curve with its baseline on it, and follows the shape when it changes; the shape stays a normal node (remove its stroke to hide it). align then places the text on the path (open path: left = from its start, center = in its middle, right = ending at its end; closed shape: starts at / is centred on / ends at the shape's starting point, which is the top of an ellipse and the top left corner of a rect, going clockwise), path_offset moves it along from there (px), path_side:true puts it on the other side running the other way (e.g. inside a circle). Letters that do not fit on an open path are hidden. The text's x / y / w / h are then derived (the box around its letters). Create the shape first: on_path needs its id.
- path: points [{x, y, in?: [dx, dy], out?: [dx, dy]}] in the same coordinate space as x/y of other nodes; in/out are bezier handles relative to the point (omit for corners). closed, fill, stroke, stroke_width, cap, join. Its x/y/w/h are derived from the points.
- image: image_path (absolute path to PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/BMP/SVG) or svg (inline SVG markup — ideal for icons and illustrations); x, y, w, h (omit w/h for natural size, or give one to keep the aspect ratio), radius, fill (optional color overlay that replaces the image's colors but keeps its alpha — use it to tint icons).
- instance: instance_of (id of a main component), x, y, and optionally w, h (its layers are laid out again by the constraints they have in the main component) and name. A linked copy of that component: it follows every later change of the main, except the properties that were changed on the instance itself (overrides). Do not give `children`: its layers come from the main and can only be restyled, with update_nodes.

Stroke ends and corners: cap (butt|round|square, default butt: the ends of a line or an open path; square reaches half the stroke width past the end point) and join (miter|round|bevel, default miter: the corners of a path, a frame, or a rect / image without radius; a miter sharper than about 29 degrees is cut off to a bevel). Canvas and export draw them the same.

Common to all: name, rotation (degrees clockwise around the center), flip_h / flip_v (rect, ellipse, image and text only: mirrors what the node shows inside its box, left-right / top-bottom, e.g. a mirrored photo or icon; to flip paths, lines, frames or several nodes together use arrange), opacity (0-1), visible, blend (normal|darken|multiply|lighten|screen|plus-lighter|exclusion), blur (layer blur radius in px, 0 or null = off; blurs the whole node with its shadow, and a frame with its contents), inner_shadow (a shadow inside the shape, over its fill and under its stroke, as {x, y, blur, color}; null = off; for shapes, closed paths, text, images and frames), background_blur (frosted glass: radius in px of the blur of whatever lies behind the node, shown inside its shape under its own fill, so give the node a see-through fill such as #ffffff33 or none; 0 or null = off; for rectangles, ellipses, closed paths, images and frames), constraints (for a node inside a frame: what it keeps when that frame is resized, as {horizontal: left|right|left_right|center|scale, vertical: top|bottom|top_bottom|center|scale}; default left / top. left_right and top_bottom keep both margins, so the node changes size with the frame; center keeps the offset from the frame's center; scale keeps the proportions. Set them when building anything that should adapt, e.g. a background left_right + top_bottom, a close button right + top, a footer left_right + bottom).

Auto layout: `layout` on a frame = {direction: horizontal|vertical (default horizontal), wrap (horizontal only: items that don't fit the width continue on a new row), gap (space between neighbours; "auto" = space_between), row_gap (between wrapped rows), padding (a number for all sides, [horizontal, vertical], [left, top, right, bottom] or {left, top, right, bottom}), align (along the direction: start|center|end|space_between), cross_align (across it: start|center|end), width, height (how the frame itself is sized: fixed = its w / h, hug = as large as its items plus padding, fill = see sizing)}. A new layout hugs on every side that was not given a w / h. Its children are the items, in array order; x / y given for them are ignored (a warning says so). Each child may have `sizing: {horizontal: fixed|fill|hug, vertical: ...}`: fill takes the room the frame has left along the direction (shared equally between the items that fill) and its whole inner size across it; it needs a frame that does not hug on that side. hug is for a child frame with a `layout` of its own (the same as its layout.width / height). Text: wrap:false text is as large as its content; wrap:true text can fill the width, its height follows the lines (unless fixed_height:true). `absolute: true` takes a child out of the layout: it keeps its x / y and follows its constraints. Hidden children are skipped. Layouts nest: e.g. a card = vertical layout, fixed width, height hug, holding a title, a text with wrap:true + sizing.horizontal fill, and a horizontal row of buttons with sizing.horizontal fill; a button = horizontal layout with padding [16, 10] and align center, holding a text. Made a main component, such a button gives instances that grow with their own label.

Colors: "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA". fill may also be null (none) or a gradient: {type: "linear"|"radial", angle (linear: 0 = left to right, 90 = top to bottom), stops: [{pos: 0-1, color}]}.

After building, call screenshot to check the result visually.

parent.description: Id of an existing frame (top-level or nested) to add the nodes into. Omit to create top-level nodes.

nodes.description: Node specs. Each needs `kind`; see the tool description for the properties of each kind.

name: update_nodes
description: Change properties of existing layers. Each entry is {id, ...properties to change} using the same property names as create_nodes; anything not mentioned stays as it is. Moving a frame moves its children. Pass `parent` (frame id at any depth, or null for top level) to move a node into or out of a frame; x/y are then relative to the new parent. A frame can be moved into another frame, but not into itself or its own content. `kind` cannot be changed. Set `component` true / false on a frame to make it a main component or a plain frame again. A layer inside an instance (it has `source`) takes changes of look and text as overrides that survive later changes of the main; its x, y, w, h, rotation, name and parent follow the main component and are rejected here. Resizing a frame (w / h) lays out its children by their `constraints`, nested frames included; pass `keep_children: true` in that entry to leave them where they are instead. Resizing an instance lays out its layers by the constraints they have in the main component. Auto layout: set `layout` (only the keys given change; null removes the layout and leaves the children where they are), `sizing` and `absolute` as in create_nodes. Whatever changes the outcome (a text, a size, visible, a new or deleted child, the order via arrange) is followed by a new layout at once, and the answer has the boxes as they end up. x / y of an item of an auto-layout frame are ignored, with a warning; to re-order items use arrange (forward / backward / front / back), to place one by hand set absolute: true. Giving w / h to a side that hugs or fills makes that side fixed. The layout of an instance is that of its main component and can't be set on it. The whole call is one undo step and is rejected as a whole if any entry is invalid. Returns the updated position and measured size of each node.

name: delete_nodes
description: Delete layers by id (deleting a frame deletes its children). One undo step. A layer inside an instance can't be deleted on its own. Deleting a main component leaves its instances as they are; they just stop following it.

name: arrange
description: Change stacking order, grouping or layout. front/back move the nodes to the top/bottom of their parent; forward/backward move one step (in a frame with auto layout this is also the order of the items: forward = one place further along the row or column). group ties two or more nodes together so they select and move as one (optional `name`); ungroup releases the groups those nodes belong to. component makes a main component: a single frame becomes one as it is, other layers (from the same parent) are wrapped in a new frame fitted around them; returns its id. detach turns instances into plain frames that no longer follow their main. reset drops the overrides of an instance, or of one layer inside it. distribute_h / distribute_v need three or more nodes: the two outermost stay where they are and the others are moved so that the gaps between neighbours are equal. tidy needs two or more: nodes that form one row or one column are aligned (top / left) and get equal gaps, anything else is snapped into a grid (rows by vertical overlap, read left to right, one column gap and one row gap). flip_h / flip_v mirror the nodes left-right / top-bottom about the center of the box around all of them: one node flips in place, several also swap sides, a frame flips with everything in it, and rotations are negated. For distribute and tidy the members of a group count as one node. Layers inside an instance can't be reordered, grouped, moved or flipped this way.

name: import_svg
description: Import SVG markup as editable layers (not as a picture; for that use create_nodes with kind image and `svg`). The result is one frame the size of the SVG (its width / height, or its viewBox), named `name`, that holds a vector path per SVG shape with fill, stroke, opacity and gradients carried over and all transforms applied; basic shapes, `use` and text (if the font is installed) become paths too, groups become Kanvas groups (one level), embedded bitmaps become image layers. Not carried over, and reported in `not_supported` by kind: masks, clip paths (other than one around the whole page), filters, pattern fills, blend modes Kanvas does not have. Stroke caps and joins are not part of the Kanvas model. One undo step. Returns the frame `id`, its size, and the number of `shapes`; read the layers with get_document.

svg.description: The SVG document as text (starts with <svg … or <?xml …).

x.description: Left edge of the frame, relative to `parent` if given (default 0).

parent.description: Frame to put it in. Omit for the top level.

name: outline_stroke
description: Outline stroke (Ctrl+Shift+O in the app): turn the stroke of each node into a filled vector path of the same shape and color, so it can be edited, united or given a gradient like any other shape. Works for rectangles (with corner radius), ellipses, lines, vector paths (open or closed, with holes, dashed) and images; inside / center / outside alignment, rotation and flips are taken into account. A shape that has a fill stays, without its stroke, and the outline is put right above it in one group with it; a shape without a fill is replaced by its outline and keeps its id. The inside border of a frame becomes the top layer in that frame. Other frame borders are skipped, shapes without a stroke are ignored. A text node among the ids is converted to vector paths of its glyphs instead (outline text; straight or on a path, with underlines, list markers, rotation and flips): one path per text color, which takes the place and the id of the text, plus one for underlines / strikethroughs, grouped when there are several; it is no longer editable as text. One undo step. Returns `outlines` (ids of the stroke outlines), `text_paths` (ids of the paths made from texts), `selected` (all of those plus the shapes the outlines belong to) and `skipped`.

name: select_nodes
description: Select layers in the app so the user can see what you mean, and by default zoom the view to them. Empty ids clears the selection and zooms to fit the whole document.

zoom.description: Zoom the view to the selection (default true).

name: screenshot
description: Render a node (usually a frame) or the whole document to a PNG and return it as an image, so you can check the design visually. Uses the same renderer as export, so it shows exactly what the user would export.

id.description: Node to render. Omit for the whole document.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels (default 1024, max 2048).

name: export
description: Export a node or the whole document to a file on disk. The format follows the file extension: .png, .jpg, .svg or .pdf. A PDF is vector (text as outlines); with `id` it has one page, without it every top-level frame of the current page becomes a PDF page (rows top to bottom, left to right). Print options: `bleed` extends the exported area on all four sides (a frame's own fill and the layers sticking out of it fill the bleed; layers outside the frame are not shown), `crop_marks` adds trim marks in a margin around it, and for PDF `color: "cmyk"` converts everything to DeviceCMYK (neutral vector colours such as black text become black ink only). A PDF with bleed or marks carries TrimBox and BleedBox. Without `icc` the CMYK conversion is a plain formula with no colour management. Returns the path and, for PDF, `pages`, `trim_size_pt` and how the colours were made.

path.description: Absolute output path ending in .png, .jpg, .svg or .pdf.

id.description: Node to export. Omit for the whole document (PDF: every frame as a page).

scale.description: Pixel scale for PNG/JPG, e.g. 2 for @2x (default 1).

bleed.description: Bleed in millimetres on every side (default 0; print shops usually ask for 3).

resolution.description: Document px per inch of paper, for the size of a PDF page and of the bleed (default 72: 1 px = 1 pt, as the Paper presets; use 300 for a design made in 300 dpi pixels, e.g. A4 = 2480 x 3508).

crop_marks.description: Crop marks at the four corners, outside the bleed (default false).

color.description: PDF only: colour of the output (default rgb).

flatten.description: PDF only: every page as one 300 dpi image instead of vectors (default false).

icc.description: PDF with color cmyk: absolute path of the CMYK ICC profile of the press; embedded as the output intent and used for the conversion.

name: pages
description: Pages of the document (like pages in Figma). Each page has its own layers; color styles, text styles and images are shared. All other tools work on the current page only, so switch first to read or edit another page. list: all pages. switch: make page `index` current. add: new empty page at the end (optional `name`) and switch to it. rename: set `name` of page `index`. duplicate: copy page `index` with all its layers and switch to the copy. delete: remove page `index` and its layers (the last page can't be deleted). `index` is 0-based and defaults to the current page. add/rename/duplicate/delete are one undo step each. Returns the page list.

name: replace_text
description: Find and replace in the text of text layers (the Find and replace window of the app, Ctrl+H). Every occurrence of `query` is replaced with `replacement`; character-range styles (`spans`) keep their place, and the text boxes, auto layouts and instances around the texts follow. Hidden and locked layers are skipped. A layer inside an instance takes the new text as an override; replacing in a main component reaches its instances that still show the main's text. The whole call is one undo step. Returns `replaced` (number of occurrences), `layers` (number of text layers changed) and `updated` (id, position and measured size of the changed layers on the current page). Use it instead of update_nodes to rename a product, fix a recurring typo or change a year across many layers.

query.description: The text to look for (not a pattern; may contain \n).

replacement.description: What to put in its place; "" removes the matches.

match_case.description: Uppercase and lowercase must match (default false).

whole_word.description: Only matches that are not part of a longer word (default false).

scope.description: page = the current page (default), all = every page.

name: library
description: The user's personal image library: logos, photos and graphics they reuse across designs (the Library window in the app). list: every item with its name and absolute `path` — pass that path as `image_path` to create_nodes to place it. Check here first when the user mentions their logo or "my" images. add: copy an image file (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP or SVG) into the library so it is available in every document. Returns the item list.

path.description: Absolute path of the image file to add (action add).

name: file
description: Document file operations. info: path and counts. new: start an empty document. open: open a .kanvas file. save: save (pass `path` for a document that has no file yet, or to save a copy elsewhere). Documents that already have a file are auto-saved by the app. new/open refuse to drop a never-saved document with changes unless discard is true — ask the user before discarding.

path.description: Absolute path to a .kanvas file (open, save).

discard.description: Allow new/open to drop unsaved changes of a never-saved document.

name: history
description: Undo or redo in the app. Every create/update/delete/arrange call is one step.

name: list_fonts
description: Search the Google Fonts catalog available in Kanvas, most popular first. Returns family name, category and available weights. Query matches the family name or category (sans serif, serif, display, handwriting, monospace).
